chunks: Ibn Nuh said: Abu Nasr Hibatullah ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Abu Ali ibn Abi Jayyad (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Ahmad al-Dallal al-Qummi narrated to me

He said: I entered upon Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) one day to offer my greetings, and I found him with a wooden tablet (sajah) in front of him and an engraver inscribing upon it and writing verses from the Quran and the names of the Imams (peace be upon them) on its margins. I said to him: 'O my master, what is this tablet?' He said to me: 'This is for my grave; it will be in it.' He said either: 'I will be placed over it' or: 'I will be raised over it.' And I knew from him that every day I descend into it and recite a portion of the Quran (in it) and ascend. And I think he said: He took my hand and showed it to me, saying: 'When it is such and such a day of such and such a month of such and such a year, I will return to Allah, the Exalted, and will be buried in it, and this tablet will be with me.' When I left his presence, I recorded what he mentioned and did not cease waiting for it, until the matter did not delay until Abu Ja'far fell ill, then he died on the very day he mentioned from the month he said from the year he mentioned, and he was buried in it. Abu Nasr Hibatullah said: I heard this hadith from someone other than (Abu) Ali, and Umm Kulthum bint Abu Ja'far (may Allah be pleased with her) also narrated it to me.

key_terms.اعْتَلَّ: To fall ill or become sick.
key_terms.حَوَاشِيهَا: The margins or sides of the tablet.
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him (a honorific used for companions/scholars).
key_terms.سَاجَةٌ: A wooden tablet or frame, often used for inscriptions or as a cover for a grave.

ai.seo_question: What sign did Muhammad ibn Uthman give regarding his death and burial place?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Qummi, a key figure among the Four Deputies (al-Safirs) of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari, demonstrating his spiritual authority through the preparation of his grave and *sajah* (wooden tablet). The narrative underscores the concept of *karamat* (miracles of the saints) and the continuity of divine guidance during the Minor Occultation, as he recites portions of the Quran daily before his predicted death. This event serves as a tangible sign of truth for the Shia community, affirming the reliability of the deputies' knowledge of the unseen.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 332 - Ibn Nuh narrates from Abu Nasr Hibtullah Ibn Muhammad, who narrates from Abu Ali Ibn Abi Jayyed Qummi, who narrates from Abul Hasan Ali Ibn Ahmad Dallal Qummi,

who said: I came to Abu Ja’far Muhammad Ibn Uthman (a.s) on a certain day to offer him my greetings. He was there and in front of him was a square frame of oak and an inscriber who was inscribing on it and writing verses of Quran and names of the Holy Imams on its sides. I asked him, “What is this tablet for, my master?” He said: “This is for my grave; it will be in it.” He said either, “I will be placed over it” or, “I will be raised over it.” Then he said: “I am done with it, and every day, I descend into it and recite a part of Quran and come back.” Abu Ali Ibn Abi Jayyed Qummi says, I also think he said: Abu Ja’far Ibn Uthman (a.s) took my hand and showed his tomb to me. He told me that on such and such day of such and such month of such and such year, I will go towards Allah, the Exalted, and will be buried here, and this frame of oak will be with me.” When I came out from his place, all his providential sayings came true. I was constantly watching his state. It was not long that he became ill and then died on the very day of the month and the year he had confided in me; and he was buried there. Abu Nasr Hibatullah says: I heard this narration from someone other than Abu Ali and in the same way Umme Kulthum binte Abi Ja’far has also narrated it to me.
